title: Select relay role alternatives across vendors
lead: Select relay role rows deterministically across vendors, expose matching alternatives, allow per-run overrides, and include the orchestrator in the role matrix. Preserve project order by default; the harness from which the owner launches the relay must not silently change the chosen lineup.
findings_note: Owner request, 2026-10-16: Codex implementer and orchestrator alternatives, automatic selection with overrides, and future bidirectional harness launching.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** launching agent processes, inspecting credentials or installed harnesses, adding SDKs or dependencies, changing the generic example's vendor policy, or implementing bidirectional Codex/Claude launch tooling. The agents repo owns the companion launch work described below.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
The owner requested Codex / OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol at medium reasoning as an alternate implementer and gpt-6.1-sol at high reasoning as an alternate orchestrator. The current recommendation selects only the first matching row per role, and the matrix cannot represent orchestrator rows. Alternatives must be usable without requiring individual model choices at every Setup.

The owner chose project-order automatic selection with optional harness preference and explicit row overrides, allowed mixed-vendor review in this project, and chose Claude Code / Claude opus at high reasoning as the default orchestrator. Keep reviewer independence: nobody who wrote slice code may review or gate it.

Scores: importance 2 because this enables the requested vendor alternatives; urgency 2 because it supports the current relay workflow; effort 2 and size M because selection, schema compatibility, CLI output, relay contracts and a TUI integration point change together. Tree slicer, pass v1.12 follows the current relay work.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/roles.py`: role schema/version, matching candidates, deterministic resolution and text presentation as needed.
- `src/slicer/ops.py` and `src/slicer/cli.py`: accept orchestrator rows through existing mutations; recommendation flags, validation and output.
- `src/slicer/mergeroles.py`: preserve new-role rows through existing schema-aware merging.
- `src/slicer/ai.py`: Setup selection instructions and shared relay contract version.
- `src/slicer/tui.py`: keep orchestrator out of the worker pipeline while preserving its existing parent/child presentation.
- `tests/test_relay_roles.py`, `tests/test_merge_roles.py`, `tests/test_ai.py`, `tests/test_tui.py`: meaningful regression coverage.
- `docs/agents.md`, `docs/commands.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`: document changed JSON/schema/relay interfaces and behavior where applicable.
- This project's role rows/rules and generated outputs: change only through worktree-local slicer CLI commands; never open or edit tracking files directly.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- Existing implementer/reviewer/gate/architect picks remain unchanged without preference or overrides; orchestrator is appended to recommendation role order.
- Every alternative satisfies the same size, effort, well-specified, split and sliver conditions as a selected row; preserve matrix order, excluding the selected row from alternatives.
- Preferred harness chooses its first matching row, and a role without a match on that harness falls back to its first matching row across harnesses. The launching harness has no implicit effect.
- Explicit selection wins over preference and matrix order. Reject duplicate role overrides, malformed selectors, unknown roles/rows, wrong-role rows and condition-mismatched rows.
- Orchestrator rows round-trip through add/set/show/recommend and merge. Old matrices load without writes; the next mutation upgrades the role schema; unsupported future versions are refused.
- JSON/text outputs are deterministic, including empty alternatives and unmatched roles under --lean; recommendation writes no tracking state or history.
- The TUI still represents the orchestrator as the parent rather than an extra worker pipeline stage.
- Relay text explains collective Setup acceptance, overrides and launch routing; shared contract markers agree across commands.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Begin implementation in a separate new worktree `/Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/slicer/.worktrees/s320`, on a new feature branch from main, before claiming the slice. Keep the working directory at `/Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/slicer` for every command. Never cd to a worktree or change the tool working directory. Use absolute paths for repository/worktree arguments, scripts, test discovery directories and scratch directories. Use `git -C /Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/slicer/.worktrees/s320 ...` and `PYTHONPATH=/Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/slicer/.worktrees/s320/src python3 -m slicer --root /Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/slicer/.worktrees/s320 ...`.
2. Write the failing tests and observe them fail before implementing. Mutation-check the new behavior tests against an incorrect selection, filtering or output implementation.
3. Add orchestrator as a valid matrix role and bump the role schema version. Load existing matrices without writes and upgrade on their next mutation. Keep their existing rows, ids, rules and order; do not automatically seed or replace their configuration.
4. Extend `relay-roles recommend` with optional `--prefer-agent AGENT` and repeatable `--select ROLE=ROW_ID`. Compare preferred agent names after trimming and casefolding; retain original display text. Select an eligible explicit override first, otherwise the first eligible row on the preferred harness, otherwise the first eligible row in matrix order. Preference is optional and run-local. All non-selected matching rows are alternatives in matrix order. No match produces a null row and empty alternatives. Recommendations remain read-only and do not launch processes or probe credentials.
5. Preserve existing top-level recommendation keys and the first four role positions, then append orchestrator. Each role entry retains `role` and `row` and adds `alternatives` (full row objects) and `selected_by` (override, preferred_agent, matrix_order, or unmatched). `unmatched` includes every role with a null row. Preserve null rows and empty alternatives under --lean. Show selected rows, selection reasons and alternatives in text output. Use established error codes: unknown row is unknown_role_row; invalid selector fields, duplicate overrides and ineligible selections are bad_role_field. Include corrective diagnostics.
6. Extend role CRUD, schema-aware merging and the necessary TUI integration. Do not add orchestrator to the worker pipeline simply because it joins the matrix role names.
7. Update Setup to obtain the resolved lineup, show it once and let the owner accept the recommendation collectively or override individual rows. Automatic selection does not bypass other Setup decisions, authorize starting paid sessions on its own, or authorize committing/landing. Preserve the routing contract: native subagents on the orchestrator's harness and headless sessions for another harness. Bump the shared relay contract marker consistently; document the change for companion tooling.
8. Through this project's slicer commands, add a generic Codex / OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol medium implementer row after existing implementer rows, plus Claude Code / Claude opus high as first orchestrator and Codex / OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol high as second orchestrator. Generic means no slice conditions on the new Codex implementer row, so it can be chosen for a whole slice, split part or sliver. Preserve all existing default implementer picks. Update this project's mixed-vendor rule to permit automatic implementation/review/gate selection across vendors, preserving reviewer independence. Do not change the generic example's vendor policy or inject this project's model choices into it.
9. Record the companion agents-repo requirement in the documentation: either Codex or Claude may be the outer entry point; both directions must preserve shared briefs/reports, explicit model/reasoning, worktree/sandbox propagation, completion/cancellation and run tracking. Actual launching requires inspecting that repo in an authorized workspace and trials in both directions. Do not claim that bidirectional launching was verified by this selection slice.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- Run affected tests, then the full suite, using the implementation worktree's absolute script/test paths and an ignored worktree-local absolute TMPDIR. Follow the project's suite timeout/background guidance.
- Run worktree-local slicer check and `git -C /Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/slicer/.worktrees/s320 diff --check`.
- Verify default recommendations preserve existing picks and select Claude opus/high for orchestrator; `--prefer-agent Codex` selects Codex medium implementer and Codex high orchestrator while retaining eligible Claude reviewer/gate choices; explicit row overrides win.
- Confirm recommendation commands do not write, and the role matrix is only changed through slicer commands.
- Read the required handoff note kind, record the verified outcome, and hand off with render/check. Keep absolute paths and the original working directory throughout.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Implementation must use its own new worktree `/Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/slicer/.worktrees/s320` and feature branch, not the filing worktree or main. Commit and land the implementation only when separately authorized by the owner. The authorization to commit and land this specification filing does not authorize implementation commits, merging, pushing or publishing. Never mark this slice done merely because its specification was filed.
